claims.claim: For the mf4090 B runs, the Day 2 plan decides that a 4M replay buffer does not fit only when the log shows an XLA RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / base limit message or a Warp out of memory message; the plan text states no whole-card peak memory threshold.

The Day 2 plan says that if the full B training runs out of memory midway it is recorded as 'B has no result' without automatically lowering the buffer, and that a fallback to a 3M buffer is decided by a human.
The training chain marked all three mf4090 B smokes as failing, and for each one the only failure reason it printed was that the whole-card peak memory (23843, 23845 and 23855 MiB) exceeded 23000.

When the memory ceiling is set to 24564 MiB, all three B smokes pass the smoke check, which includes having no RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or base limit message in the log, a final checkpoint at the expected step count, and the Day 1 image fingerprint.
Before the run, the mf4090 smoke queue noted that the B real-time smoke was lengthened past the first curriculum stage and a checkpoint save because the memory margin was only about 0.9 GB.
The B real-time smoke's latest complete checkpoint is at 36,001,792 steps.
The training chain reported that the B real-time smoke crashed with a RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error.
